chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Shu'ayb, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'What is the limit of the patient when he is convalescing during the Fasting?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'That is up to him. He is more knowing of himself. When he is strong, so let him Fast'.
ai.seo_question: When should a recovering patient resume fasting during Ramadan?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) emphasizes the principle of *al-a'lam bi-nafsihi* (he is more aware of himself), granting the sick person autonomy to judge their recovery rather than relying on a fixed medical threshold. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential preference for ease (*taysir*) and individual discretion in lifting the exemption of illness, provided the person is no longer in danger. It reflects the broader legal maxim that uncertainty is resolved by the individual's own reliable assessment of their physical state.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Shuayb, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What is the limit of the patient when he is convalescing during the Fasting?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘That is up to him. He is more knowing of himself. When he is strong, so let him Fast’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus ibn Shu’ayb from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the limit of the illness that weakens one when fasting. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is up to him to decide; he knows better about his soul and when he is strong he can then fast.’”
